text: Alexandrine Parakeet (Psittacula eupatria) Family: Psittaculidae. Genus: Psittacula. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Resident. Habitat: Dry and moist deciduous forest, evergreen forest edge, riverine woodland, plantations, orchards, agricultural mosaics and urban parks with mature trees; sea level to 1000 m. Length: 56–62 cm. Wingspan: 54–62 cm. Weight: 200–300 g. Size: 56–62 cm. Conservation status: Near Threatened. IUCN status: Near Threatened. Large long-tailed parakeet of dry and moist deciduous forest, riverine woodland, plantations, orchards and urban parks with mature trees; sea level to 1000 m.

Alpine Accentor (Prunella collaris) Kashmiri name: Zanda tsar. Family: Prunellidae. Genus: Prunella. Category: Songbird. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Resident (altitudinal migrant). Length: 15–18 cm. Wingspan: 25–30 cm. Weight: 25–40 g. The Alpine Accentor is a winter migratory bird frequently observed within the cold deserts, alpine regions and high-altitude wetlands of Ladakh within forests, gardens and woodland habitats. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Amur Falcon (Falco amurensis) Family: Falconidae. Genus: Falco. Category: Raptor. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Rare Visitor. Length: 28–31 cm. Wingspan: 63–71 cm. Weight: 97–155 g. The Amur Falcon is considered a rare visitor occasionally sighted across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley across mountains, cliffs and open valleys. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Asian Paradise Flycatcher (Terpsiphone paradisi) Kashmiri name: Fhambaseer. Family: Monarchidae. Genus: Terpsiphone. Category: Songbird. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Summer Migratory. Habitat: Moist and dry deciduous forest, riverine and riparian woodland, bamboo groves, plantations and large tree-lined gardens, often near water; 0–2400 m. Length: 19–22 cm. Wingspan: 25–30 cm. Weight: 17–22 g. Size: 19–22 cm. Conservation status: Least Concern. IUCN status: Least Concern. Medium-sized monarch flycatcher, summer breeding visitor to Kashmir; male with glossy black crested head, blue eye-ring, white or rufous morph and very long ribbon tail streamers; female rufous above with greyish throat and shorter tail; hawks insects with agile sallies under the forest canopy in deciduous and riverine woodland, bamboo and large gardens.

Barn Owl (Tyto alba) Kashmiri name: Rata Mogul. Family: Tytonidae. Genus: Tyto. Category: Owl. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Resident. Length: 33–39 cm. Wingspan: 80–95 cm. Weight: 250–700 g. Size: Medium. The Barn Owl is a resident bird species commonly found across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley inside forests and rocky landscapes. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Black-hooded Oriole (Oriolus xanthornus) Family: Oriolidae. Genus: Oriolus. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Resident. Habitat: Open woodland, forest edge, plantations, orchards, gardens and cultivation with fruiting trees (especially figs); lowlands to 1200 m. Length: 23–25 cm. Wingspan: 35–40 cm. Weight: 46–79 g. Size: 23–25 cm. Conservation status: Least Concern. IUCN status: Least Concern. Bright yellow oriole with a solid black hood, black wings and tail centre and a pinkish-red bill; open woodland, forest edge, plantations and gardens; eats figs, berries and insects in the canopy.

Black-naped Monarch (Hypothymis azurea) Family: Monarchidae. Genus: Hypothymis. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Resident. Habitat: Moist and dry broadleaf forest, forest edge, secondary growth, bamboo, riverine woodland and well-vegetated gardens near forest; lower and mid canopy, shaded perches; 0–1800 m. Length: 16 cm. Wingspan: 20–24 cm. Weight: 10–14 g. Size: 16 cm. Conservation status: Least Concern. IUCN status: Least Concern. Small azure-blue monarch flycatcher (male with black nape patch and narrow black breast band, whitish belly; female duller, blue-grey head, brownish upperparts, lacking the black markings); sits upright on shaded low to mid-canopy perches and sallies for flying insects, often joining mixed-species foraging flocks; moist and dry forest, forest edge and bamboo of the Jammu foothills.

Black Kite (Milvus migrans) Kashmiri name: Gont. Family: Accipitridae. Genus: Milvus. Category: Raptor. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Resident. Length: 55–60 cm. Wingspan: 135–155 cm. Weight: 560–940 g. Size: Large. The Black Kite is a resident bird species commonly found across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley across mountains, cliffs and open valleys. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Blossom-headed Parakeet (Psittacula roseata) Family: Psittaculidae. Genus: Psittacula. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Resident. Habitat: Lowland and foothill forest (evergreen, semi-evergreen and dry deciduous), forest edge, secondary growth, bamboo thickets and wooded farmland; sea level to 1500 m. Length: 30 cm. Wingspan: 40–45 cm. Weight: 85-90 g. Size: 30 cm. Conservation status: Near Threatened. IUCN status: Near Threatened. Parakeet of lowland and foothill forest, forest edge, secondary growth, bamboo thickets and wooded farmland; sea level to 1500 m.

Common Kingfisher (Alcedo atthis) Kashmiri name: Kola tonch. Family: Alcedinidae. Genus: Alcedo. Category: Kingfisher. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Resident. Length: 16 cm. Wingspan: 25 cm. Weight: 34–46 g. Size: Small. The Common Kingfisher is a resident bird species commonly found across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley across diverse habitats. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Common Myna (Acridotheres tristis) Family: Sturnidae. Genus: Acridotheres. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Resident. Length: 23–26 cm. Wingspan: 36–43 cm. Weight: 82–143 g. The Common Myna is a resident bird species commonly found across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley across diverse ecological habitats. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Eurasian Hoopoe (Upupa epops) Kashmiri name: Satut. Family: Upupidae. Genus: Upupa. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Summer Visitor. Length: 25–32 cm. Wingspan: 44–48 cm. Weight: 46–89 g. The Eurasian Hoopoe is a summer visitor bird species commonly found across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley across diverse ecological habitats. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Greylag Goose (Anser anser) Kashmiri name: Ans. Family: Anatidae. Genus: Anser. Category: Goose. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh. Migratory status: Winter Migratory. Length: 74–91 cm. Wingspan: 147–180 cm. Weight: 2,160–4,560 g. The Greylag Goose is a winter migratory bird frequently observed across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley near lakes, marshes and wetlands. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Himalayan Monal (Lophophorus impejanus) Kashmiri name: Sunal, Suna Murg, Haum. Family: Phasianidae. Genus: Lophophorus. Category: Other. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Resident. Length: 61–76 cm. Wingspan: 85–95 cm. Weight: 1,800–2,380 g. The Himalayan Monal is considered a rare visitor occasionally sighted within the cold deserts, alpine regions and high-altitude wetlands of Ladakh across diverse ecological habitats. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.

Kashmir Flycatcher (Ficedula subrubra) Family: Muscicapidae. Genus: Ficedula. Category: Songbird. Region: Jammu, Kashmir Valley. Migratory status: Summer Migratory. Length: 13 cm. Wingspan: 19–21 cm. Weight: 9–12 g. IUCN status: Vulnerable. The Kashmir Flycatcher is a summer migratory species recorded across the wetlands, forests and river systems of Kashmir Valley within forests, gardens and woodland habitats. This species contributes to the rich avian biodiversity of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh.
